title: client IP trust through the Caddy+ngrok proxy chain (and the per-IP rate limiter it feeds)
expected: client_ip() records the real internet caller's address (and the shared /account/* rate limiter buckets by that real address, not by a value every public user shares)
note: root cause: Caddy appends its OWN immediate-peer address (always local, since the ngrok agent connects to it over loopback) as the last X-Forwarded-For hop; client_ip() trusts exactly that last hop, discarding the real client IP ngrok itself already injected earlier in the header. Effect: the 30-req/300s auth rate limiter (config.py auth_rate_limit_attempts) is a single GLOBAL budget shared by every public caller, not a per-attacker throttle -- any one user's traffic (malicious or not) can lock everyone else out of login/register/refresh for the window; and audit log client_ip is forensically useless for anything that came through this chain.

No real Stripe Checkout Session, customer, or payment ever existed for this org
note: app/services/stripe_webhook_service.py:_apply_checkout (around line 201-208) reads plan_id from session.metadata and accepts it once _plan_known() confirms it names a real plan; there is no cross-check against the price/amount in the forged line items, and no server-side record of which plan a REAL checkout session for this org was meant to grant. Suggested fix: when applying a checkout completion, derive the plan from the Stripe price id on the line item (as _apply_subscription already does via _plan_for_price), not from client-set metadata, or record the intended plan server-side when the Checkout Session is created and match against that id instead of trusting metadata on the event

title: Row-Level Security provides NO protection in this deployment: the app DB role is a Postgres superuser with BYPASSRLS
expected: with BUILDER_RLS_ENABLED=true and RLS enabled+forced on organizations/projects, a query run as the app's own database role, with app.organization_id correctly set to org A, should see ONLY org A's rows
actual: LIVE-CONFIRMED against the real throwaway Postgres container: created two disposable orgs (A, B) each with one project via the real API; temporarily ALTER TABLE ... ENABLE/FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY on organizations and projects (reverted immediately after, see note); ran 'SET app.organization_id = <org A id>; SELECT * FROM projects;' as the builder role -- it returned BOTH org A's AND org B's project, not just org A's. Root cause: SELECT rolname, rolsuper, rolbypassrls FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname='builder' -> (builder, true, true). PostgreSQL NEVER applies row-level security to a superuser or a role with BYPASSRLS, regardless of FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY -- there is no override for this. The policy itself is correctly written (verified via pg_policy: exactly the expected USING clause) and BUILDER_RLS_ENABLED=false in this env currently anyway (so RLS is not even turned on at the app-settings level right now) -- but the finding is deeper than 'RLS is off': even if every switch in app/core/rls.py were flipped on today, RLS would still protect NOTHING, because the specific role BUILDER_DATABASE_URL connects as bypasses it structurally
note: app/core/rls.py's own docstring says "We never grant BYPASSRLS to the app role" -- that intention is not what is actually configured for this environment's database role. Before going live: (1) create a dedicated, narrowly-scoped Postgres role for the running application that is NOT superuser and does NOT have BYPASSRLS (migrations can keep using a separate, more privileged role); (2) only then is RLS actually a second wall of defense rather than a no-op. Test reverted cleanly: ALTER TABLE ... NO FORCE / DISABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY run immediately after, confirmed back to relrowsecurity=false on both tables; no data read, written or exposed beyond this session's own two disposable test orgs/projects

title: the MCP endpoint is completely unreachable through the public-facing URL (421 Invalid Host header), independent of authentication
expected: an MCP client reaching the app at its real public URL (the same origin every REST route works on) should get the same routing/auth treatment as the REST API, not a transport-level rejection before any app code runs
actual: LIVE-CONFIRMED, reproduced twice: POST /mcp (a plain, unauthenticated 'initialize' call) through the public ngrok tunnel -> 421 'Invalid Host header'. The IDENTICAL request sent directly to the Caddy proxy on 127.0.0.1:8081 (bypassing only ngrok) -> 200, normal MCP response. grep of app/api/mcp.py shows no allowed_hosts/transport-security configuration at all -- the mcp package's Streamable HTTP transport applies its own default Host-header allow-list (a DNS-rebinding defense, sane for local dev) and the app never widens it to include settings.public_api_url's real hostname
note: Impact if unaddressed: MCP (a billed, plan-gated feature -- plans.allow_mcp, max_mcp_tokens) is NON-FUNCTIONAL for every customer reaching the app through its real public URL, which is every real deployment behind any reverse proxy/CDN/tunnel with a different Host header than the backend's own bind address -- not a corner case, the normal case. This is a product-availability bug with a security-adjacent root cause (Host validation), not itself exploitable, but worth fixing before MCP access matters for real customers. Suggested fix: configure the mcp library's transport security / allowed hosts from settings.public_api_url's hostname (and likely settings.public_app_url's too, for completeness) in build_mcp_app()

actual: code-confirmed: app/services/mcp_service.py:102 -- the shared _check_project_access helper (used by every tool) checks 'if org.require_mfa and not principal.mfa_satisfied: raise org_mfa_required(...)', the exact same check org_context uses for REST routes (Principal.mfa_satisfied for an api_token is user.mfa_enabled). Live repro deferred to a future pass pending the same org/account setup as authn/mfa/2.5

title: what an unauthenticated internet client can reach on the public origin
expected: no debug/metrics endpoint, no stack trace, only intentionally-public discovery endpoints
actual: LIVE-VERIFIED against the tunnel: /health=200 {status:ok} (minimal); /ready=200 {status:ready} (minimal); /metrics=404; /debug=404; /openapi.json=404; /docs=404; /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource=200 (RFC 9728, intentionally public, lists scopes only); /sso/metadata/<slug>=200 for a real org slug (SAML SP metadata -- entityID/ACS-URL/NameID-format only, no secret, this is meant to be IdP-fetchable); /scim/v2/* (Users, ServiceProviderConfig, Schemas, ResourceTypes) all 401 without a bearer -- notably stricter than SCIM's own RFC 7644, which allows unauthenticated discovery of those last three, so not a gap

title: NOTES item 2 confirmed live: password login/signup works on a domain with an active, verified SSO org ("enforce SSO" is not built)
expected: an account on a domain that has a verified SSO-active org should either be blocked from password sign-up/login, or the app should document this as an accepted gap
actual: LIVE-CONFIRMED: registered a brand-new disposable account at sectest-ssogap-<random>@dumbpotato.com (dumbpotato.com is bb-sso's real, verified SSO domain) via plain POST /account/register -> 201; immediately logged in with that same password -> 200, full session token. Code-confirmed too: platform_auth_service.login() has no reference to SSO/org domain policy anywhere in its path. Matches NOTES_FOR_TEST_SESSIONS.md item 2 exactly -- a known, already-documented gap (agent_5/agent_6), not a new regression
note: Only affects accounts that have never SSO-signed-in (their password is still real; once a password account SSO-signs-in once, its password is wiped -- see item 9/9). Suggested fix (tracked as a known gap already, not newly discovered): an org policy to refuse password login/signup for its verified domain(s) once SSO is active, with a break-glass admin override

title: NOTES item 5 confirmed by code: invitation (and all app) mail has no Date or Message-ID header, a classic spam-filter trigger
expected: outbound mail should carry Date and Message-ID so mainstream mail providers treat it as a normal message rather than flagging it
actual: code-confirmed: app/services/mail_service.py:_send_sync() builds an email.message.EmailMessage() setting only From/To/Subject + body, then calls smtp.send_message() directly -- smtplib does NOT auto-add Date or Message-ID (unlike some higher-level mail libraries), and neither is added by this code. Matches the setup session's observed symptom (GoDaddy filed the app's invite mail under Spam) exactly
note: Easy fix: message["Date"] = email.utils.formatdate(localtime=True); message["Message-ID"] = email.utils.make_msgid()

title: NOTES item 6 confirmed by design, not a bug: an invitation is created even if the e-mail send fails
expected: n/a -- this is an explicit, documented design trade-off, not an oversight
actual: code-confirmed: app/services/mail_service.py's own module docstring states "Best effort by design: an invitation is valid whether or not the e-mail goes out, and the admin always gets the link once in the API response." The 201/"created but maybe not emailed" behavior observed in setup is this documented trade-off working as intended; whether the UI clearly surfaces a "created but not emailed" state is a session-2 (feature test) concern, not a security finding

title: NOTES item 9 confirmed by code: the password-wipe-on-IdP-claim pre-hijack mitigation is ONE shared function, used uniformly by SAML, OIDC, JIT-into-existing-account, AND SCIM-linking
expected: Session 1 should verify the password/session reset on IdP claim also happens for OIDC, SCIM-linked accounts, and JIT into an existing account, not just the SAML case already observed in setup
actual: code-confirmed: app/services/platform_auth_service.py:claim_by_idp() is called from exactly two call sites -- sso_service.py:1130 (the single sign-in-completion path shared by BOTH finish_saml() and finish_oidc(), covering a brand-new JIT account AND an existing account being claimed, since the user-lookup-or-create happens above this line for both protocols identically) and scim_service.py:462 (SCIM user linking). Because it is the SAME function reused everywhere rather than three separate reimplementations, the SAML case already observed live in setup (credentials_reset: true) gives high confidence the others behave identically -- not independently live-verified this session for OIDC/SCIM specifically, due to the domain/mail constraints noted throughout this report

title: 33 mutation checks run in a scratch copy against the full current test suite: 31 killed, 2 survivors (both explainable, not new gaps)
expected: a security-relevant code change (disabling a check, flipping a guard, weakening a comparison) should make at least one existing test fail
actual: Ran review/tests/mutate.py (now 33 mutations, up from the prior review's 21 -- Phase F additions for impersonation/RLS/export) in a full rsync scratch copy (/tmp/.../scratchpad/mutate_scratch, never the working tree) against a disposable Postgres database ('mutate_test' in the throwaway bb-final-pg container, dropped after). 31/33 KILLED. Survivors: (1) M09 'audit detail sanitizer off' -- SURVIVED, 130 passed. This reproduces the prior review's F-009 exactly: _FORBIDDEN_DETAIL_KEYS=() leaves every existing test green; the canary test (test_adv_secrets-style) finds no ACTUAL leak today because nothing currently puts a secret in an audit detail, but the sanitizer control itself has no dedicated unit test, so a future code change that starts logging something sensitive in 'detail' would not be caught. Still open. (2) M14 'project member must be org member off' -- SURVIVED, but this is a WEAK mutant: it only renames the error CODE STRING ('not_an_org_member' -> '..._X'), not the actual guard logic on that same line. The real logic-equivalent mutation, M16 (same underlying `if in_org is None:` check, flipped to `if False:`), WAS killed (1 failed, 54 passed) -- so the control itself is solidly tested; M14 just shows no test asserts the exact string value of that one error code, which is not a security property
note: Full per-mutation results in final_test/sec-test-sonnet-5/logs/mutate.log. This reuses and extends review/tests/mutate.py (33 mutations now vs 21 at the prior review -- Phase F additions for impersonation/RLS/export were added since)
